terms.grammar: adverb, interrogative and relative, of motion towards
evidence: Hor. S. 1.9.62–63: unde venīs et quō tendis?
terms.comment: English “where are you going?” asks quō, never ubi. As a relative it answers eō, (to) there.

terms.gloss: in what direction? (and) to what end?
evidence: Ter. Eun. 304: neque unde eam neque quōrsum eam
Hor. S. 2.7.21: quōrsum haec tam pūtida tendant (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From quō vorsum; also “what is it leading to?”: quōrsum haec?

phrases.english: where have you come from, and where are you heading?

phrases.latin: Quō abīs? manē; manē, inquam: quō abīs?
phrases.english: Where are you going? Wait; wait, I tell you: where are you going?

phrases.latin: Abī deambulātum. — Deambulātum quō? — Vah! quasi dēsit locus.
phrases.english: Go for a walk. — A walk where? — Pah! As if there were nowhere to go.

phrases.latin: nesciō hercle, neque unde eam, neque quōrsum eam
phrases.english: I really don’t know where I’m coming from or where I’m going

sources: Lewis & Short: quo · Lewis & Short: quorsum
